end.summary: Practised representing 11–20 as one bundle of ten and loose ones.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised counting from ten and adding loose ones, using sticks and eggs as examples. They connected two loose sticks with two cycle tyres and later formed thirteen as ten and three. Saanvi still mixed up the bundle being called “one” with its value of ten; this was explained and used correctly for thirteen, but the idea was not yet consistent. At home, build a bundle of ten small objects and add 1–9 loose objects, saying both the bundle count and its value.
